proof_summary: Quadratic reciprocity makes 5 a quadratic residue modulo p; choosing the even root r among complementary roots and setting n=r-1 and q=(r^2-5)/p gives q odd, q≤n-1, and gcd(q,2(n-2))=1 (a common divisor of q and r-3 must divide 4). An integer recurrence for the continued fraction gives its relevant numerator as n^2+2n-4=pq and shows that q divides the accompanying denominator while p does not, so reduction cancels exactly q and leaves p.
